first.rationale: The concurrent declines in onboarding completion and activation make onboarding simplification the most directly evidenced, durable lever for restoring early adoption and supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Verify the two relevant archived records before committing, while keeping the test guarded because current-quarter drivers and segment effects remain uncertain.

mid.rationale: Run a standard, guarded shortened-onboarding experiment for self-serve accounts. The verified record shows completion +13%, time-to-value down 2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%, directly addressing both current declines while supporting sustainable revenue. Use retention and qualified-revenue guardrails, since the related SMB signup-simplification result showed a 1% retention decline despite revenue lift.

final2.rationale: Continue the already-selected guarded onboarding-simplification experiment rather than replace it with promotional pricing. The deeper competitor cut and doubled SMB churn conversations raise urgency, but the available evidence says promotional pricing materially harms 30-day retention and should not be generalized as a sustainable-growth response. Shortened onboarding has verified gains in completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention; monitor price-sensitive SMB churn and qualified revenue as guardrails.
